resources.string: This screen is currently rendering at %1$s — %2$s will be upscaled from that, not true %2$s detail. If your device supports a higher screen resolution, raising it in Android\'s own Display settings (not just here) is the only way to get more real source detail.
10-bit only adds real detail on HDR content — on ordinary (SDR) screens and apps, which is most of them, it will look the same as 8-bit but may cost more battery or fall back automatically.
SOFTWARE AV1 IF NO HARDWARE (AV1 ONLY)
When on, and this device has no hardware AV1 encoder, recording uses a CPU-based AV1 encoder instead of switching to a different codec — capped at 1080p, and noticeably hotter/slower than hardware.

Ducks the mic when system audio it just played appears to be bleeding back into it acoustically (loud speaker, no headset). STRONG cuts harder/faster for stubborn cases; OFF disables this layer (platform echo cancellation, if the device has one, still runs).

A normal app can\'t keep its own on-screen controls both visible live and cleanly excluded from its own recording — see GUIDE. VISIBLE keeps the small bubble reachable the whole time; AUTO-HIDE shows it briefly then detaches it (reach it again from the notification); BLACKOUT keeps it reachable but replaces it with a small solid black shape in the recording.

Type your preferred prefix in the template box to personalize your saved video titles. Add the {timestamp} placeholder to ensure every file is organized sequentially by date. Invalid characters are stripped automatically, defaulting to a clean timestamp if empty. Format: yyyyMMdd_HHmmss (e.g. 20260712_143000).
%1$s · tap to open, or use the floating controls
RecorderX needs the \"draw over other apps\" permission so the pause/stop controls can float on screen during recording, without pulling down the notification panel.
Microphone permission denied — recording system audio only.
No hardware video encoder matched these settings; falling back to the most compatible software encoder. Expect higher CPU use.
No hardware AV1 encoder on this device — recording real AV1 anyway using a CPU-based (software) encoder, capped at 1080p. Expect higher heat/battery use than hardware encoding.
10-bit isn\'t supported by this device for the selected codec — recording in 8-bit instead.
%1$s isn\'t supported on this device — recording with %2$s instead.
%1$d fps isn\'t sustainable at this resolution on this device — recording at %2$d fps instead (resolution is kept, never shrunk, to hit an fps target).
This device\'s encoder can\'t reach %1$s — recording at %2$s instead (the codec\'s own capability, not a fallback to a different codec).
Device is warming up — bitrate automatically reduced to about %1$d%% to manage heat. Quality will recover once it cools.
Device cooled down — bitrate back to normal.
No audio was captured — check that microphone permission is granted, and that the app/game you\'re recording allows its audio to be captured.
System audio unavailable this session (the app you\'re recording may not allow audio capture) — recording microphone only.
Microphone unavailable this session — recording system audio only.

Tip: recording system audio + mic through the phone\'s own speaker can let game/media audio bleed back into the mic. Suppression is active, but a wired or Bluetooth headset avoids the bleed at the source for the cleanest result.
Storage permission is needed to save recordings on this Android version.
Couldn\'t start recording on this device (no usable encoder or output location).

1) Pick your video and audio settings below — Bitrate updates automatically as you change Resolution/FPS/Codec.
2) Tap Start Recording, then grant screen-capture and (if you enabled a mic source) microphone permission.
3) Use the small floating bubble to pause, resume, or stop — it's kept small and out of the way, its eye icon fully hides it whenever you want a completely clean frame, and Bubble Visibility further down lets you trade reachability for cleaner frames (or accept a small black shape instead).
4) A recording made on a phone whose screen is genuinely running below your chosen Resolution will be upscaled, not sharper — a note appears under Resolution when that's the case.
5) Files save to Movies/RecorderX and are named from your Output Template.

No normal app — this one included — can make its own on-screen controls both fully visible live and fully invisible in its own recording at the same time; that's a platform limit, not a setting we haven't added yet.
